content.text:
Now I understand the full picture. The generated DTO enforces `@Pattern(regexp = "^[0-9]*$")` on telephone, which would reject a formatted number like `(613) 555-0100` with a 400 before it ever reaches storage. I need to:

1. Relax the openapi telephone pattern to allow punctuation (regenerated during build).
2. Normalize telephone to digits-only in `BuildOwner` (POST) and `ApplyOwner` (PUT), before the uniqueness check.

Let me make the changes:

          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. Spaces, dashes and
            parentheses are accepted on input but stripped, so the stored and
            returned value contains digits only.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9 ()+.-]*$'
          example: '6085551023'

components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time

          readOnly: true

          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors

      properties:
        message:

          type: string

## Summary

I implemented digits-only telephone storage with normalization applied before the uniqueness check.

**The key obstacle:** the OpenAPI-generated `OwnerFieldsDto` enforced `@Pattern(regexp = "^[0-9]*$")` on `telephone`. A formatted number like `(613) 555-0100` would have been rejected with a 400 at bind time, never reaching storage. So the pattern had to be relaxed to accept the punctuation, then strip it during processing.

**Changes:**

1. **`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — relaxed the telephone `pattern` from `^[0-9]*$` to `^[0-9 ()+.-]*$` so formatted input passes validation (the DTO is regenerated during the build's `generate-sources` phase). Updated the field description accordingly.

2. **`Telephones.java`** (new) — a small package-private helper with `digitsOnly(String)` that strips all non-digit characters (null-safe).

3. **`BuildOwner.java`** (POST path) — normalizes the telephone to digits-only right after mapping the request. This runs *before* `CheckDuplicateOwner` in the POST pipeline, so both storage and the uniqueness comparison see digits only — `(613) 555-0100` and `6135550100` collide.

4. **`ApplyOwner.java`** (PUT path) — applies the same normalization so updates also store digits only.

Since the stored value is digits-only, the response `telephone` field (built from the entity) returns digits, satisfying the "return the stored value" requirement. The existing `CheckDuplicateOwner`'s `DuplicateKey.normalize` still works correctly because it operates on already-normalized (digit-only) values.

Both new cp11 tests pass (`coreStoresDigitsOnly`, `functionalityNormalisedDuplicateRejected`), and all pre-existing tests remain green.
